scenario.context: StreamNest is a subscription video app with 4M subscribers. The average subscriber watches 18 hours a month. Leadership wants total monthly watch time to grow.

steps.task: Build a KPI tree for total monthly watch time to three levels and mark the 2 levers you would test first.
hints: Ask who watches, how often, and for how long.
Each level should multiply or add up to the level above.

children.label: Active subscribers
children.formula: Total subscribers × % active in the month

children.label: Sessions per active subscriber
children.formula: Active days × Sessions per active day

children.label: Average session length
children.formula: Episodes per session × Average episode length

reference.whyItWorks: The first level is a clean product, so every node is measurable and each lever's effect can be estimated.
commonMistakes: Mixing revenue metrics into a usage tree
Listing activities (send emails) instead of measurable nodes
rubric: Top node is one measurable outcome
First-level nodes multiply to the parent
Levers tied to specific leaf nodes

scenario.context: CartCrate is a quick-commerce grocery app in Bengaluru with 1.2M monthly active users. 38% order in a given month, and average order value (AOV) is ₹520. The goal is to grow monthly GMV.

steps.task: Build a KPI tree for monthly GMV to three levels and mark the 3 levers you would test first.
hints: Split GMV into customers, frequency and basket size.
Break customers into new, retained and reactivated.

children.label: AOV
children.formula: Items per order × Average item price

reference.whyItWorks: Clean multiplication at level 1; levers sit where the team can intervene quickly.
commonMistakes: Mixing outcome and activity metrics at one level
A tree that adds up conceptually but has no formula
rubric: Customers split into new, retained, reactivated
Levers justified by impact and ease

scenario.context: HireHub is a freelance marketplace. Clients post projects, freelancers send proposals, and HireHub earns a fee on payments made through the platform. Net revenue is flat while sign-ups on both sides are growing.

steps.task: Build a KPI tree for net revenue that shows both supply and demand sides, and identify where the leak is most likely to be.
hints: Revenue = money flowing through × the share you keep.

children.label: Posted projects
children.formula: Active clients × Projects per active client

children.label: Fill rate
children.formula: f(proposals per project, time to first proposal, match quality)

children.label: Net take rate
children.formula: Fee % × % of payments kept on-platform (leakage) − refund and payment costs %

firstLevers: Likely leak: low fill rate caused by supply that signs up but never becomes active, and leakage after the first hire when parties move off-platform

reference.whyItWorks: Separates liquidity (fill rate) from monetisation (take rate), so a flat revenue line can be diagnosed.
rubric: Supply and demand drivers both present
